div.div:
Credentials
All ten <service>_runtime passwords belong to the OpenBao database engine: one static role per runtime, rotated every 720 h by that cluster's vault_rotator (one openbao-db-config Job per cluster). External Secrets reads database/static-creds/<service>-runtime through the openbao-db store every 15 s into a Secret in the cluster namespace and in the service namespace; pods mount it and read DB_PASSWORD_FILE, and the DatabaseRoles carry no passwordSecret. OpenBao KV (store openbao, hourly) holds the migrators, db_authz, vault_rotator, Temporal and Keycloak. Neither pooler holds a password: PgDog passes each login through to product-db, PgBouncer looks it up with auth_query over a client certificate. Every service, worker, migration and authz hop verifies the homelab-ca server certificate (verify-full); Keycloak, Temporal, OpenBao and pgroles do not yet (#1296, #1306). Backups authenticate to RustFS with pg-backup-rustfs-credentials.

div.div:
Why the DR replica reads from RustFS
product-db-replica never connects to the primary: it bootstraps from product-db's base backup and then replays its WAL archive from the bucket, so it survives the loss of the product-db pods. Its designated primary keeps its own archive and a daily backup in product-db-replica/ (7 d). Migrations always target the -rw service directly, never a pooler.
